title: Global fragment compaction and cross-request KV slice reuse
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Problem: For latency-sensitive workloads we observe duplicated KV cache data across concurrent requests that share overlapping prompt prefixes. This increases GPU memory pressure and reduces effective batching density. Goal: implement a global fragment compaction layer that identifies and reuses shared KV slices across requests (and across GPU contexts when pinned to the same device) while preserving correctness for causal generation and per-request KV lifetimes.
technical_notes:
High-level plan:
1) Introduce an immutable, content-addressed fragment format: small contiguous KV 'slices' created at tokenization boundaries. Each slice gets a short fingerprint (XXHash64) and a reuse score computed from observed overlap.
2) Maintain a per-device global registry mapping fragment fingerprint -> memory handle + refcount + last_used_epoch. Registry supports cross-request lookup at enqueue time so that new requests can reference existing slices instead of allocating duplicates.
3) Implement a lightweight merge-on-pin operation that maps a request's KV pointers to the shared slice memory region; for model code this is transparent (same KV layout).
4) Eviction: combine LRU windows with reuse score and estimated recompute cost to prefer retaining high-benefit slices. Eviction triggers compaction of fragmented GPU regions to avoid fragmentation.
5) Continuous batching integration: when building batches, prefer grouping requests that already reference the same slices to reduce memory churn and increase batching TTL.
Concerns and mitigations:
- Correctness: slices must include sequence and position metadata to ensure they are applied to the right key/value indices during generation. Add unit tests that replay mixed-length requests and assert identical logits as the baseline.
- Locking: use lock-free reference counting and epoch barriers to avoid introducing global contention in the hot path.
- Migration: support a fallback path that copies KV data into the request-local arena if a shared slice is evicted mid-generation.
- Metrics: add reuse_hit_ratio, slice_pull_latency, and shared_memory_frag_pct to console instrumentation.
tasks: Design immutable fragment format and fingerprint schema
Implement device registry API and refcounting primitives
Hook registry lookup into request enqueue and continuous batch builder
Implement merge-on-pin pointer mapping and runtime tests
Eviction policy: LRU+reuse-score implementation and compaction routine
Add observability: metrics, tracing spans, and console dashboard tiles
Benchmarking: end-to-end throughput/latency runs with synthetic overlap workloads
Write migration docs and rollout plan with feature flag gating
acceptance_criteria: Reusable fragments yield >= 25% average GPU KV memory reduction on overlap-heavy workloads
End-to-end p95 generation latency regresses < 5% compared to baseline in mixed workloads
No correctness regressions across 1000 randomized replay tests (deterministic logits)
Metrics available in Console: reuse_hit_ratio, shared_memory_frag_pct, slice_evictions
Feature behind runtime feature-flag and can be disabled without service restarts
Documented rollback steps and a simple migration checklist for Dedicated/Private customers
comments: 2026-02-11 - Sofia Alvarez: Initial spike showed a 37% duplicate allocation rate on a conversational benchmark. Captured heap profiles and sample traces (attached to confluence).

2026-02-20 - Marcus Li: Prototype registry implemented (local-only) and validated cross-request lookup in a microbench. Observed a 12% reduction in peak GPU allocator churn. Next: make it device-global and add refcounting semantics.

2026-03-01 - Performance: Ran scale test with 2000 concurrent short-turn chats; reuse_hit_ratio hovered around 0.42 for median traffic. Memory compaction introduced a 3% CPU overhead but reduced fragmentation by ~18%.

2026-03-08 - Design review notes: PM asked for additional telemetry to correlate reuse hits with user session IDs (privacy review required). Also recommended exposing a knob for minimum fragment size to trade off lookup overhead vs reuse benefit.

2026-03-12 - Marcus Li: Merged PR #8421 with registry and lookup hooks behind feature flag. Edge-case: when using mixed quantized variants, pointer mapping requires variant-aware handles — flagged as follow-up (ENG-34405).
